title: softdown-translator-and-slo-tethering-hotfix
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Fix: introduce 'softdown-translator' to avoid abrupt circuit flips during transient region overloads; SLO tethering to limit degradation scope.
description:
Motivation: During last week's regional degradation incident we observed rapid circuit flips when a cascading egress pressure spike hit a subset of nodes. The result was oscillating failovers and noisy telemetry spikes that caused several short-lived SLO breaches. This PR introduces a small runtime shim ("softdown-translator") that translates aggressive circuit state transitions into timeboxed, telemetry-anchored softdown windows and tethers SLO relaxation to a bounded budget.

What I changed (high-level):
- New softdown translator component in the routing stack that receives raw circuit events and emits 'softdown' directives. Softdown directives temporarily reduce SLA expectations for a tenant/cohort but do not immediately trigger cross-region failover.
- SLO tethering: a budgeted counter per-tenant/cohort that caps cumulative softdown time over sliding windows (configurable default 10m/1h). This prevents unlimited silent degradation from eating into customer SLOs.
- Telemetry anchoring: each softdown is stamped with the triggering metrics snapshot (latency p50/p95, token queue depth, kv-cache pressure) so downstream observers and the console can correlate degradations with root signals.
- Backstop hotfix: an emergency unwind path that forces immediate circuit reset if softdown windows exceed a safety threshold (to avoid stuck softdown states after controller crashes).

Design notes:
- The translator is conservative: it aggregates identical circuit-flip events from the same region for 250ms before emitting a softdown. This coalescing reduces noise from connection churn.
- Softdown directives carry a reason code (eg: "egress_surge", "kv_pressure", "probe_timeouts") used by the console and rollback policies.
- SLO tethering budget operates on two axes: per-tenant and per-region. Per-tenant budgets prevent noisy tenants from hogging softdown credits; per-region budgets prevent a single region from silently defaulting to a degraded state across customers.
- Configs are feature-flagged and default to disabled for Dedicated/private installs; the hosted control plane enables a conservative default.
